Subject: Private control plane: SSO/SCIM rollout and IAM role mapping plan

Hi Alice and team,

Thanks again for the sync earlier — this thread is to consolidate the plan for integrating Acme's IdP with our private control plane (VPC/on-prem deployment) and to align on the SAML assertions, SCIM attributes, and IAM role mappings we need for the first rollout. Key goals:

- Enable SSO for the Redwood control plane console (SAML 2.0)
- Implement SCIM provisioning for user + group sync (incremental provisioning)
- Establish cross-account IAM role trust (if Acme prefers cloud-brokered access) or service-account mapping for on-prem nodes

Attached: iam_role_mapping_v1.xlsx (mapping + suggested role names), scim_schema_v2.csv (attribute set), private-controlplane-network-diagram.png (network readiness notes).

Proposed timeline:
- 10/11 – configuration in Acme Okta test org, SAML metadata exchange
- 10/13 – SCIM test provisioning (subset of 5 users + 2 groups)
- 10/15 – end-to-end login + session auditing test (test SAML + SCIM together)

Open questions for Acme:
1) Do you want group-to-role mapping done on your side (Okta push groups) or would you prefer Redwood to apply mappings based on SCIM group attributes?
2) For access to on-prem inference nodes, do you want cross-account IAM roles (AWS) or local service accounts with mTLS?
3) Any constraints on attributes we send in SAML (e.g., employeeNumber, eduPersonAffiliation)?

Please review the attachments and share any redlines. Dev, could you draft the minimal trust policy and a SAML assertion example we can hand to Acme?

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — looks good. A few quick clarifications from Acme security: 

- We prefer group-to-role mapping to be driven from Okta (push groups) so our identity team retains control. Is Redwood able to accept Okta group push via SCIM or do you need mapping tables in your config?

Hi Alice — great, thanks for the preferences. Quick responses inline: 

- Okta group push vs Redwood mapping: Redwood can accept SCIM group push (we consume group.displayName and group.members). We also support an internal mapping table for edge cases (e.g., when multiple external groups map to one Redwood role). For this rollout, group push sounds simplest. I'll mark that preference in the runbook.
- mTLS for on-prem: noted. We'll prepare certificates and a service-account workflow for your infra team.
- acmeRole: yes, we can consume acmeRole as a custom SAML attribute and use it during session creation and authorization checks. Please include it in the SAML attribute map.

Attached is a lightweight SAML & SCIM checklist I created (see scim_schema_v2.csv for fields). Dev — can you paste a simple IAM trust policy + SAML assertion example in this thread so Acme's Okta admin has what they need?

Next steps: I'll update the Confluence runbook and share the test accounts list by 10/06.

Thanks,

Hi all — putting a technical example here that Acme's Okta admin can copy. This assumes two integration modes: (A) cloud-backed cross-account role (AWS) or (B) on-prem mTLS + local service account.

(A) Example minimal AWS trust policy for a role that accepts SAML assertions from Acme Okta (replace {IDP_ARN} and {SAML_PROVIDER_ARN}):

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"Federated": "arn:aws:iam::{ACME_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}:saml-provider/{ACME_SAML_PROVIDER}"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {"SAML:aud": "https://signin.aws.amazon.com/saml"},
        "ForAnyValue:StringLike": {"SAML:attribute:acmeRole": ["infra_admin","data_scientist"]}
      }
    }
  ]
}

Notes: we recommend constraining by acmeRole where possible, and using Audience restriction. NameID should be EmailAddress format. For session names, we set role_session_name to the user's email.

(B) For on-prem mTLS: Redwood will issue a short-lived client certificate tied to a service account. The control plane enforces CN=service-account:<acme-team> and maps that to a Redwood role (see iam_role_mapping_v1.xlsx). Workflows: Acme admin requests cert via CSR to Redwood SRE (we can automate later).

SAML assertion sample (attributes we expect):
- NameID (Format:urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress) -> user email
- urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User:username -> username (optional)
- acmeRole -> string (used for RBAC)
- groups -> multivalued list

I'll attach an updated iam_role_mapping_v1.xlsx with role -> group mapping examples.

If Acme wants, we can also spin up a short-lived test endpoint for SCIM calls to validate provisioning behavior before you flip production.

-Dev
